reason: Both catch the same four core defects (WHERE clause killing the LEFT JOIN, UTC/local-day mismatch, integer division truncation, NULL-vs-zero totals), but B adds a genuinely useful and correct consequence directly tied to this query — that NULL total_spent values will sort to the top under ORDER BY ... DESC in engines like Postgres, misrepresenting zero-spend customers as top spenders. A's extra point (non-aggregated columns without full GROUP BY) is a much weaker addition since A itself concedes it may not actually be broken in the relevant engine, making it a hedged portability note rather than a concrete defect.
